about: Verdict store mutants (lawcache): how an entry reaches the disk.

mutants.name: lawcache-write-in-place
mutants.rule: An entry is built beside its place and published by one rename: a reader never meets half of it.

mutants.name: lawcache-shared-part-name
mutants.rule: Each writer builds its entry in a file of its own: two writers of one key never mix their texts; the last rename wins whole.

mutants.name: lawcache-key-unframed
mutants.rule: A kept entry is served only for the very parts it was kept under: no join or split of parts finds it.

mutants.name: lawcache-fresh-reads-disk
mutants.rule: check and test --fresh read no entry another run kept, and still keep their own passes.

mutants.name: lawcache-within-escapes-root
mutants.from: if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
mutants.rule: Only a path below the request's module folder is written relative to it; any other path stays absolute.

mutants.name: lawcache-names-unresolved
mutants.from: return err == nil && resolved != root && strings.Contains(text, resolved)
mutants.to: return err == nil && resolved != root && false
mutants.rule: An answer that names its module folder, as written or with links resolved, is not kept under a key that names no workspace.
